---
title: "Retained scenario and simulation handoffs"
---

WF3 publishes a reusable scenario collection. WF4 selects explicit run IDs from
a ready collection, runs Wflow-SBM against a completed WF1 model, and retains
native responses for later indicator requests. WF2 projection analysis is an
independent plausibility overlay and does not select stress-test scenarios.

| Handoff | Published under `project_dir` | Consumer |
|---|---|---|
| Scenario collection | `scenarios/<collection_id>/` for generated series and lookups; `scenarios/_engine/collections/<collection_id>/collection.json` for the inventory | WF4 selects a ready collection and explicit run IDs. |
| Simulation responses | `experiments/<experiment_name>/hydrology/wflow/output/`, with `experiments/<experiment_name>/_engine/response_inventory.json` | Indicator reduction reads retained native Wflow responses. |
| Indicator set | The experiment's `_engine/indicator_sets/<indicator_set_id>/` (`indicators.json`, `data/` tables and lookups, coverage evidence) | Result readers join indicator tables to their run-group lookup and request metadata. |
| Named indicator set | `experiments/<experiment_name>/results/indicator_sets/<set-id>/` (tables, lookups, `indicators.csv`), committed by `_engine/indicator_sets/names/<set-id>/current.json` | Post-processing reads one set's readable view after the workflow finishes. |

The collection, simulation, and indicator set have separate identities. A changed
collection, model, or simulation setting requires a new experiment. A changed
indicator request creates another indicator set from retained responses without
rerunning Wflow. Published products are validated before reuse and are not
silently overwritten.

## Startup input checks

When WF4 is enabled, the all-workflow runner checks the experiment request before launching WF0,
then rechecks inputs before each enabled workflow handoff. These checks compare configuration,
templates, local input hashes and scientific code identities. Catalog checks compare parsed source
YAML and its root location: explicit `meta.root`, the first existing `meta.roots` candidate, or the
catalog directory. A newly available preferred root is therefore detected even when the YAML bytes
have not changed. Unchanged YAML bytes reuse parsed documents; files and root locations are read again.

The launcher does not load HydroMT for these checks. Catalog expansion, driver/adapter validation and
forcing-unit verification occur in the consuming workflows. Invalid adapter definitions can therefore
be reported when their workflow starts rather than during experiment admission.

Experiment requests retain catalog source YAML and root context. Reuse requires the current source
root and scientific inputs, including producer code, to match the recorded request. A different root
is refused rather than guessed or rewritten. Changed scientific code requires a new experiment;
records and results remain intact. Collection identity also depends on scientific code, so automatic
seeds can change when that code changes.

For a stable post-processing path, WF4 publishes each selected indicator set to
`experiments/<experiment_name>/results/indicator_sets/<set-id>/` after each invocation, including reuse.
Each set's committed inventory is `_engine/indicator_sets/names/<set-id>/current.json` within the
experiment; sets commit independently. Read these copies after the workflow finishes; the hashed
indicator sets remain immutable.

WF3 similarly mirrors the selected collection's full contents directly into `scenarios/`, including
lookup CSVs, `series/`, `config/`, and `weathergenr/`.
Its tracking metadata is `scenarios/_engine/current.json`. These are mutable post-processing copies;
the immutable scenario collection remains the WF4 handoff.

Use the owned launchers: `scripts/run_workflows.py` for generation and
`scripts/simulate_system.py` for simulation. The
[WF3 workflow](workflow-generate-scenarios.qmd),
[WF4 workflow](workflow-simulate-system.qmd), and
[output guide](../guide/outputs.md) give the current controls, paths, and join
keys.
